title: Intelligence artificielle et objets connectés | l'EPSAA et la Mairie de Paris
learners_amount: 608 learners have completed this activity in the past 12 months.
star_rating: Average rating of 4.5 stars by 8 learners in the past 12 months.
description:
About this learning activity

Explorant l’Histoire, Luc Julia revient sur les grandes étapes de l’émergence de l’intelligence artificielle. Il cite la Pascaline, créée en 1645, une machine d’arithmétique mise au point par Blaise Pascal qui marque le début de la computation. Cette machine permettait de faire des additions et des soustractions à quatre chiffres en deux secondes, ce qui à l’époque était extraordinaire. « C’est la première machine qui augmente l’intelligence de l’homme », note Luc Julia. Il évoque ensuite Basile Bouchon qui, en 1725, invente le ruban perforé, qui a été conçu pour programmer les machines à tisser. 1956 est une autre date clé, avec la tenue d’une Conférence, au Dartmouth College (USA), au cours de laquelle John McCarthy emploie pour la première fois le terme d’intelligence artificielle. Luc Julia définit ensuite la notion de machine learning, des machines qui ont la capacité d’apprendre, puis le deep learning, « où la machine a l’opportunité de définir des paramètres », ce qui va mener à la reconnaissance visuelle, de la parole, etc.

Ce MOOC est proposé par l'EPSAA et la Mairie de Paris. 
 
Après avoir suivi cette activité, revenez sur cette page et sélectionnez " Marquer terminé" afin de prendre en compte ce parcours.

Note : cette activité est uniquement disponible en français.

description:
Welcome! This learning plan provides the background and skills necessary to be ready to contribute to Call for Code for Racial Justice open source projects. In response to the murders of George Floyd, Ahmaud Arbery, Breonna Taylor, and too many others, Black IBMers had a vision to make use of technology to address social injustice. Their top ideas have been released as open source projects through the Linux Foundation.

This learning plan contains resources to help you learn about these projects and how you can start contributing to the technology solutions, even if you do not have a technical background. Use the resources found here to get inspired, grow your skills, and finds ways you can contribute, no matter your area of expertise.
  • Learning activities: There are some required modules to make sure you know the basics about Call for Code for Racial Justice projects and open source contribution, but most modules are optional. You can explore general information about the program, technical materials, professional skills resources, or dive deep into information about one or more of our open source projects that interest you most.
  • Audience: Call for Code for Racial Justice invites problem solvers to contribute to technology solutions that directly benefit organizations doing grassroots work and local communities that need these solutions. Whatever your skills, there are valuable ways for you to participate. This learning plan is designed for anyone who is interested in how technology can be used to make a meaningful change and looking to gain skills to be ready to contribute.
  • Prerequisites: You do not need any previous programming or other experience to take this learning plan.
  • Duration: Varies. Depending on your interests and previous experience, you can complete the right combination of modules for you to build your skills.
  • Language: English

Remember to:
  • Review the first section to learn about the program and explore more on the topics of racism, racial equity, and racial justice.
  • Pay particular attention to details on joining the Call for Code for Racial Justice community to stay connected and benefit from community expertise and networking.
  • Consider taking the Introduction to Open Source course if you’re brand new to open source projects to learn about key concepts, tools, and processes that you need to start contributing to any open source project. You can earn a badge by completing this course!
  • Check out the Design Thinking course to learn about techniques you should apply to keep your impacted users at the center of the solution you design. You can earn a badge by completing this course!
  • Dive into the details about any of the seven Call for Code for Racial Justice open source projects.
  • Learn about the technology building blocks used in our open source projects, if you are interested in making a technical contribution.

This plan is a starting point, and we encourage you to stay curious and explore additional resources as needed.

À la fin de ce cours, vous serez capable de : 
  • expliquer ce qu'est l'intelligence artificielle ;
  • identifier ses défis et ses opportunités ; 
  • décrire scientifiquement un projet d'IA et ses sous-disciplines. 

Prérequis : ce cours s’adresse à tous les citoyens qui s’interrogent sur l’intelligence artificielle, souhaitent s’informer et s’instruire. Aucun prérequis n’est nécessaire
